claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions. Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you asking about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes I'm asking about my son Alex. He's 21 and doesn't live with me anymore, but I still help him out financially when I can. I was wondering if I might still be able to claim Child Benefit for him?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information about Alex.

To assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to understand his current situation a bit better. Since Alex is 21 years old, this is a key factor.

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?**

(For context, Child Benefit can normally continue for children aged 16-19 if they're in approved education or training, but once a child turns 20, eligibility generally ends even if they're still studying.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in any education or training at the moment. He finished school a while back and he's just been trying to figure out what to do next, you know, looking for work and that sort of thing.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Let me make sure I have a complete picture of Alex's situation:

**When did Alex turn 20 years old?** 

I need to understand the timeline here, as this will help me determine if there was any period when you may have been eligible for Child Benefit before he turned 20.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Oh, he turned 20 last year actually. So he's been 21 for a little while now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. I now have enough information to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Based on what you've told me:
- Alex is 21 years old
- He turned 20 last year
- He is not currently in approved education or training
- He no longer lives with you
- You help him out financially when you can

Let me provide you with my assessment:

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'm sorry, but **you are not eligible** to claim Child Benefit for Alex.

Here's why: Child Benefit is normally available for children under 16. For young people aged 16 or over, it can continue until they turn 20, but only if they remain in approved education or training. Since Alex is 21 years old, he's beyond the maximum age limit for Child Benefit eligibility, even though you continue to help him financially.

While it's wonderful that you support Alex when you can, unfortunately the financial help you provide doesn't extend the age limit for Child Benefit purposes.

If you have any other questions about benefits or your situation changes, please feel free to ask.
